credit_metrics.text: EBITDA increased by {{ebitda.change@FY2024}} to {{ebitda@FY2024}}, and operating profit rose by {{operating_profit.change@FY2024}} to {{operating_profit@FY2024}}.
Total debt was stable at {{total_debt@FY2024}}, so gross leverage held at {{gross_leverage@FY2024}}, well below the peer median of {{gross_leverage.peer_median@2024}}.
FFO rose by {{ffo.change@FY2024}} to {{ffo@FY2024}}, but free cash flow declined by {{fcf.change@FY2024}} to {{fcf@FY2024}} as capital spending absorbed more of the cash generated.
Profit for the year increased by {{profit.change@FY2024}} to {{profit@FY2024}}.

liquidity_funding.text: The group fully repaid its interest-bearing financial liabilities, which the report says greatly reduces the potential effect of interest rate changes on the company.
Total debt of {{total_debt@FY2024}} is small against EBITDA of {{ebitda@FY2024}}, so ratios to debt say little about the credit profile.
A financing commitment was given for the City Air Terminal joint venture's new train sets, part of which was drawn as a loan in the year.

operating_performance.text: Passengers rose by {{passengers.change@FY2024}} to {{passengers@FY2024}}, but traffic growth of {{traffic_growth@FY2024}} was well below the {{traffic_growth@FY2023}} of FY2023.

Aeronautical revenue per passenger increased by {{aero_revenue_per_passenger.change@FY2024}} to {{aero_revenue_per_passenger@FY2024}}, helped by the temporary inflation-linked adjustment of airport charges.

peer_positioning.text: Gross leverage of {{gross_leverage@FY2024}} is the lowest of the airport peers ({{gross_leverage.peer_rank@2024}}), against a peer median of {{gross_leverage.peer_median@2024}}.
On EBITDA margin the company sits in the middle of the group at {{ebitda_margin@FY2024}} ({{ebitda_margin.peer_rank@2024}}).
Capex intensity of {{capex_intensity@FY2024}} also places it in the middle of the group, in line with the peer median.
Traffic growth of {{traffic_growth@FY2024}} is the weakest of the group ({{traffic_growth.peer_rank@2024}}), below the peer median of {{traffic_growth.peer_median@2024}}.

snapshot.text: Flughafen Wien, the Vienna airport group that also holds Malta and Košice airports, grew revenue by {{revenue.change@FY2024}} to {{revenue@FY2024}} in FY2024, with the complete repayment of interest-bearing financial liabilities leaving the balance sheet largely insulated from rate moves.
The EBITDA margin was broadly unchanged at {{ebitda_margin@FY2024}}, a move of {{ebitda_margin.change@FY2024}}, while gross leverage stayed at {{gross_leverage@FY2024}}.
The point to watch is capital spending: capex intensity rose by {{capex_intensity.change@FY2024}} to {{capex_intensity@FY2024}}, and free cash flow fell by {{fcf.change@FY2024}} to {{fcf@FY2024}}.

watch_items.text: Investment: capex intensity rose by {{capex_intensity.change@FY2024}} to {{capex_intensity@FY2024}}, in line with the peer median, and free cash flow fell by {{fcf.change@FY2024}} to {{fcf@FY2024}}.
Traffic: growth of {{traffic_growth@FY2024}} is the weakest of the airport peers ({{traffic_growth.peer_rank@FY2024}}), below the peer median of {{traffic_growth.peer_median@2024}}.
Regulation: airport charges are temporarily adjusted by average inflation, a rule that ends at the end of 2026, so revenue per passenger depends on the tariff formula that follows.
Litigation: disputes with the Maltese government and employee claims concerning Malta International Airport are outstanding, which the group considers unfounded.
